disclosure: Precomputed counter-arguments over checked-in demo evidence. Used whenever the live Skeptic is unavailable. These outputs never set scores, routes, blockers, approvals, or outcomes.

outputs.headline: Heat and a single televised match explain most of this movement without any brand-specific demand shift.

challenges.claim: Weather and match attention rose together, so neither record separates a genuine change in confidence-under-pressure behaviour from ordinary seasonal sweating during a widely watched event.
challenges.wouldChangeDecisionIf: The same language appears in a comparable week with no match and no heat spike.

challenges.claim: Commerce progression is positive but small enough to be consistent with normal week-to-week variation, so it cannot yet corroborate the attention signal.
challenges.wouldChangeDecisionIf: Matched treatment and comparison cells show a gap outside normal variation.

challenges.claim: Consumers describe the need without naming a brand, so the language may be a category-level observation that any competitor could answer equally well.
challenges.wouldChangeDecisionIf: Consumer language shifts toward brand-specific requests rather than the need alone.

outputs.headline: Sustained search interest may stay informational and never become a paid routine.

challenges.claim: Persistent search can reflect ongoing curiosity or media coverage rather than a change in what people actually buy and use.
challenges.wouldChangeDecisionIf: Repeat purchase or repeat-intent evidence appears alongside the search persistence.

challenges.claim: Described routines are invented aggregates in this demo, so they illustrate a behaviour pattern rather than evidencing one.
challenges.wouldChangeDecisionIf: Observed routine data replaces the synthetic stand-in.

outputs.headline: One creator family carries the whole spike, which is what paid seeding looks like.

challenges.claim: Attention concentrated in a single source family is indistinguishable from a seeded or novelty-driven spike without independent corroboration.
challenges.wouldChangeDecisionIf: A second, unrelated source family shows the same pattern.

challenges.claim: No accompanying commerce movement means the visible activity has not yet touched category behaviour at all.
challenges.wouldChangeDecisionIf: Category search or commerce progression follows the attention spike.

outputs.headline: Prior-year conversion in this window may be the promotional calendar rather than the occasion.

challenges.claim: Festive windows are also discount windows, so last year's conversion cannot separate the occasion from the price that ran alongside it.
challenges.wouldChangeDecisionIf: Prior-year conversion holds after adjusting for promotional depth.

challenges.claim: Being ready is not the same as being needed; readiness records establish that the brand can act, not that acting will change anything.
challenges.wouldChangeDecisionIf: Matched unexposed cells show lower offtake than exposed ones.

challenges.claim: A search pattern that repeats every year is predictable rather than informative, so it may add no decision value over simply running the window as planned.
challenges.wouldChangeDecisionIf: This year's search deviates measurably from the seasonal norm.

outputs.headline: Responding may hand the claim more reach than staying silent would.

challenges.claim: Amplification is a real cost: a brand response introduces the claim to people who had not encountered it, and the evidence measures spread without measuring who has actually seen it.
challenges.wouldChangeDecisionIf: Reach is measured among category buyers rather than in the aggregate.

challenges.claim: Rising ingredient-safety search may reflect general curiosity rather than doubt about this category, so the exposure may be smaller than the volume suggests.
challenges.wouldChangeDecisionIf: Search intent is separated into reassurance-seeking and avoidance-seeking.

challenges.claim: Having approved substantiation makes a response possible but does not make it persuasive; a correction that reads as defensive can confirm the suspicion it answers.
challenges.wouldChangeDecisionIf: A comparable prior episode shows response outperforming silence.

outputs.headline: Frozen dessert rises with temperature every year, so this may be seasonality a campaign would take credit for.

challenges.claim: Weather and category sales move together by default, so neither record separates a campaign-addressable moment from the ordinary shape of summer.
challenges.wouldChangeDecisionIf: The spike exceeds the same-week baseline from prior heat-waves.

challenges.claim: Narrowing to well-stocked cells fixes the service risk but also selects the cells most likely to perform anyway, which will flatter the result.
challenges.wouldChangeDecisionIf: Comparison cells are matched on days-cover as well as on baseline conversion.

challenges.claim: Days-cover is measured before the campaign exists, so it describes current demand rather than the demand a campaign would create.
challenges.wouldChangeDecisionIf: Service level is projected under campaign load rather than at rest.

outputs.headline: Monsoon dullness talk may be a weather complaint rather than a purchase intent.

challenges.claim: People describe dull skin in the monsoon every year without changing what they buy, so the language may be seasonal commentary that needs no brand response at all.
challenges.wouldChangeDecisionIf: Purchase or basket behaviour moves alongside the dullness language.

challenges.claim: Resolving ownership assumes the moment is worth owning; if the effect is small, the portfolio has spent a decision on a question that did not matter.
challenges.wouldChangeDecisionIf: The overlapping campaign already running shows a measurable incremental effect.

challenges.claim: The conflict penalty is a configured number, not an observation, so the margin between the top two candidates rests on an assumption rather than on evidence.
challenges.wouldChangeDecisionIf: Observed cannibalisation between the two brands is measured instead of assumed.

outputs.headline: Sustained pH interest may be reading rather than buying.

challenges.claim: Persistent search can reflect ongoing coverage and curiosity rather than a change in purchase criteria, in which case the claims risk is taken for no demand.
challenges.wouldChangeDecisionIf: Purchase behaviour is observed among people using pH language.

challenges.claim: The cited litigation concerned a competitor's comparative advertising, so it establishes that this territory is contested rather than that any particular claim would fail.
challenges.wouldChangeDecisionIf: Legal review assesses a specific proposed claim rather than the category in general.

challenges.claim: Substantiating a claim takes long enough that the discourse may have moved on before the work completes, making this a durable trend that is nonetheless never actionable.
challenges.wouldChangeDecisionIf: The same language persists through a second substantiation cycle.

outputs.headline: Recommendation reach can lead category search, so this may be a real signal caught too early.

challenges.claim: Flat search over seven days is consistent both with an empty signal and with a real one that has not yet surfaced, and this evidence cannot distinguish them.
challenges.wouldChangeDecisionIf: The same measures are taken again seven days later.

challenges.claim: Basket attach is a blunt instrument for a hack that may use a product people already own, so absence of attach movement is weak evidence of absence of effect.
challenges.wouldChangeDecisionIf: Usage frequency is measured rather than purchase.

challenges.claim: The concentration figure is an attribution estimate, and attribution across platforms is unreliable enough that the penalty it drives may be overstated.
challenges.wouldChangeDecisionIf: Reach is measured directly outside the originating platform.
